Here are quick, high‑impact ways to stretch your phone’s battery:

- Find the culprits: In Settings > Battery, check which apps are draining most and limit or uninstall the worst offenders.
- Screen savings: Lower brightness, shorten screen timeout, use dark mode (great on OLED), disable Always‑On Display/Raise to Wake if available.
- Radios & signal: Prefer Wi‑Fi over cellular; turn off 5G when not needed; disable Bluetooth/GPS when unused; avoid hotspot; use Airplane Mode in poor‑signal areas.
- Background cuts: Turn off Background App Refresh/auto‑sync for nonessential apps, limit push notifications, and restrict battery usage for power‑hungry apps.
- Power modes: Enable Low Power/Battery Saver whenever you’re below ~40% or expect long gaps between charges.
- Streaming/commute: Download podcasts/music for offline listening; lower streaming quality; for live streams, plug into a charger and close other apps.
- Charging care: Keep the phone cool (remove thick case if it gets hot while charging), use certified cables, avoid full discharges; try to stay roughly 20–80%. If Battery Health (if available) is <80%, consider a battery replacement.
- On the go: Since you already use compact pouches, a small power bank like the Anker PowerCore 5000 or Mophie Powerstation Mini (previously suggested) fits well and covers a full top‑up.

Great plan. Here’s a quick, targeted checklist for the store:

- Define the target sound: Try guitars that cover your core tones (your Strat’s snap vs. a Les Paul’s mid‑push). If “Blackbird”‑style fingerpicking matters, test clarity on arpeggios.
- Neck feel first: Compare 50s (chunkier) vs. 60s (slimmer) Les Paul necks; check nut width and fret size for fingerpicking comfort.
- Scale length & tension: Strat (25.5") vs. Les Paul (24.75") feels looser—see which helps your touch and open‑tuning stability.
- Weight & balance: Some Les Pauls are heavy. Play standing with a strap to check shoulder comfort and neck dive.
- Pickups/electronics: Try PAF‑style humbuckers for warmth; test models with coil‑split/tap for single‑coil‑like sparkle. Also try P‑90 options if you want bite.
- Hardware: Smooth, stable tuners; solid bridge; quiet pots/switches. Check tuning stability with bends and open D retunes.
- Open‑tuning check: Bring a tuner. Retune to open D in‑store, verify nut slots don’t bind, check intonation up the neck, and listen for sympathetic buzzes.
- String gauge/action: Ask to try or simulate your planned gauge (heavier for open D). Ensure low‑noise, comfortable action for fingerpicking.
- Test method: Play clean first (chords, arpeggios, dynamics), then add your typical gain. Try both neck and split positions for “Strat‑ish” chime.
- Unplugged resonance: Strum unplugged—feel sustain and body resonance; it often translates when amplified.
- Practicals: Ask about setup included, return window, and minor nut/intonation tweaks for open tunings.

Quick, practical ways to keep the kitchen tidy:

- Keep counters clear: use your utensil holder to group by task (stirring, flipping, serving), purge duplicates, and put the most‑used tools front and center. Add dividers and small containers (mason jars) for tiny items; stand long tools upright to use vertical space. Label sections and clean the holder regularly.
- Add wall hooks or a rail for ladles/tongs to free up counter and drawer space.
- Granite care: wipe daily with a soft cloth/stone‑safe cleaner, avoid harsh/abrasive products, use cutting boards and coasters/pads, and reseal periodically to prevent stains.
- Garbage disposal: deodorize weekly—1/2 cup baking soda + 1 cup vinegar, rinse hot; or grind ice with a tablespoon of rock salt; finish with citrus peels. Always run cold water during use.
- Fix little leaks fast: turn off water supply, check/clean the aerator, replace worn O‑rings/gaskets, tighten handle screws. Prevent drips that lead to grime buildup.
- Do a 5–10 minute nightly reset: clear and wipe counters, load/run the dishwasher, and set out what you need for tomorrow so clutter doesn’t accumulate.

Here are quick wins to level up your slow‑cooker results:

- Cut liquid by ~30–50% vs stovetop; slow cookers don’t evaporate much.
- Don’t overfill; keep it 1/2–2/3 full for even heating.
- Brown meats and aromatics first; deglaze the pan into the pot for extra flavor.
- Layer smart: dense roots at the bottom, proteins/beans in the middle; add delicate veg in the last hour.
- Keep the lid closed; every peek can add ~15–20 minutes.
- Season late. Add fresh herbs and a splash of acid (lemon, vinegar) at the end for brightness.
- Thicken at the finish: cornstarch slurry, mash some veg/beans, or crack the lid and reduce 20–30 minutes.
- For stews: use chuck, cut carrots/potatoes larger so they don’t go mushy; add dairy at the end.
- For veg/vegan dishes: bloom spices in a little oil first; boost umami with tomato paste, soy/tamari, miso, dried mushrooms, or kombu.
- For yogurt (incl. cashew): use a thermometer—heat dairy to 180–185°F, cool to 110–115°F; incubate undisturbed 8–12 hrs. For cashew, blend very smooth, strain, and consider a little agar/pectin if you want a firmer set.
- Calibrate your cooker: do a “water test” on Low/High once to learn its real temps/timing.
